1.w: The wicked flee and no one is pursuing, and the righteous are confident as a young lion.

2.w: In the transgression of the land, many [are] its princes; and with one man understanding [and] knowing, so it will last long.

3.w: A man being poor and oppressing the lowly ones [is like] a rain beating down and [there is] no bread.

4.w: Those abandoning instruction praise a wicked one, and those guarding instruction contend with them.

5.w: Men of evil do not understand justice, and those seeking YHWH understand all.

6.w: Better one being poor walking in his integrity, than one crooked in [his] ways, and he [is] rich.

7.w: One watching over the law [is] a discerning son, and one associating with gluttons disgraces his father.

8.w: The one multiplying his wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one showing favor to lowly ones.

9.w: One turning aside his ear from hearing instruction, even his prayer is an abomination.

10.w: One causing the upright to stray onto a path of evil, into his pit he himself will fall, and the blameless ones will inherit good [things].

11.w: A rich man [is] wise in his own eyes, and a poor one being discerning will search him out.

12.w: In the rejoicing of the righteous [is] great beauty, and in the rising up of wicked ones, a man hides himself.

13.w: One covering his transgressions will not prosper, and one confessing and forsaking [them] will find mercy.

14.w: Blessed [is] the man being reverent continually, and the one hardening his heart will fall into distress.

15.w: A roaring lion and a rushing bear, [is] a wicked ruler over a poor people.

16.w: A leader lacking [in] understanding [is] also abundant of oppressions; one hating dishonest gain prolongs days.

17.w: A man pressed down by the bloodshed of a soul will flee into the Pit, [with] none grabbing hold of him.

18.w: One walking blamelessly will be saved, and one crooked in [his] ways will fall at once.

19.w: The one working his land will be filled [with] bread, and the one pursuing empty [things] will be filled with poverty.

20.w: A man of faithfulness [has] an abundance of blessings, and the one hurrying to be rich will not be acquitted.

21.w: To regard faces [is] not good, and over a morsel of bread a strong man will transgress.

22.w: A man of an evil eye is panicked for wealth, and he does not know that poverty will come upon him.

23.w: The one rebuking a man, afterward he will find favor more than one being smooth of tongue.

24.w: One robbing his father or his mother and saying, “There is no transgression,” he [is] a companion to the man bringing ruin.

25.w: Being wide of appetite stirs up strife, and one trusting upon YHWH will be made fat.

26.w: The one trusting in his heart, he [is] a fool, and the one walking in wisdom, he will be delivered.

27.w: One giving to the poor will not lack, and one hiding his eyes [has] an abundance of curses.

28.w: With the rising up of the wicked, a man hides himself, and with their perishing the righteous multiply.
